assumptions_verified: Kent et al. arXiv:2104.11717v4 Table I (PDF p.5), IQT1 steps 7-9: A computes c = b XOR z and sends it to B; B sends c to B_i for i in {0,1}; B_i computes d~_i in the causal past of Q_i; caption: steps 1-8 lie in the intersection of the causal pasts of the presentation points. Fig.1 caption (p.4): message c may go to B0 or B1 and is relayed B -> B0, B1.

G's s_money_sites already TIMED the relay correctly (A0 -> B0 at L0, B0 forwards c to B1; B_b validates only once c and x are both present). No timing correction needed. Reproduces Jiang 2024 15.337 us (Jinan) and 304.207 us (Yiyuan-Mazhan).
Jinan zero-processing H1 local validation = 27.66 us = Jiang's published classical 2L/c_fibre reference (SI Table S2).
corrections_found: G engine trace DAG (qmint/networks/simulator.py): effects were parented ONLY on their trigger, with no per-actor process order. So in S-money, B_b's verification_result_available_local was NOT a causal descendant of the relayed c (Kent Table I steps 8-9) whenever c arrived no later than the token, and the trace did not show the Stage-II dependency. Fixed by adding each actor's previous event as an extra causal parent (Lamport happens-before; the trigger stays first). All G tests still pass; the round-trip detector's results are unchanged.

Frozen fixture tests/fixtures/contracts/network_two_site.json (NOT edited: not owned) declares 33356.4 ns for 10 km. The light cone is 33356.4095 ns, so the link is 0.0095 ns superluminal and G's engine refuses it. Lane-H tests now use an exact light-cone net2. Proposal: change the fixture to 33356.41 (round up).
H's lightcone_network rounded link bounds to 3 decimals, sometimes BELOW the light cone, which G's engine rejects. It now uses G's lightcone_links (exact). This removes the duplicate builder logic.

H's old direct-call H3 late-commit scenario decided a t=0 presentation as if Activate/RelayC had already arrived, which was time-inconsistent. On the engine the verifier holds the presentation until the Stage-II message lands, and local latency is measured from the later of the two. Published numbers are unchanged (stage_ii 83356.41 / 383564.10 ns).
known_limitations: S-money security is not simulated (G's model treats validity as symbolic). S1 latency rows are timing only; no epsilon is claimed.

Matched processing: every classical node step costs p (1.507 us or 0). H1 pays p at the terminal twice plus at the coordinator; relays (S-money B0, H3 issuer) cost 0. The zero_processing rows isolate pure communication.
H2 on two sites places 2 of 3 replicas at L0, so the quorum is local to L0 (best case). No leader election.
H3 preassigned and H4+H3 bind the site at issuance to the later b. That is the best case: they actually lose late choice.
RIPE: per-message delays are resampled per seed and the rng stream differs by protocol message count, so medians over 20 seeds are compared rather than paired samples.
H6 classical_bytes in benchmark_records now include the deposit message (old H number excluded it). Other byte counts move by a few bytes.
